Arijit Singh is an Indian singer and composer. He rose to prominence whilst working as a playback singer, and has been described by critics as one of the most-influential and commercially successful vocalists in Indian music. Singh is noted for his emotive vocal style and work across multiple genres.
Singh began his career in 2005 as a contestant on the reality television programme Fame Gurukul. He worked as a music programmer and assistant to composers including Pritam, Mithoon, Shankar Ehsaan Loy, and Vishal–Shekhar, and made his playback-singing debut in Hindi cinema with "Phir Mohabbat". He gained wider recognition in 2013 with "Tum Hi Ho" from Aashiqui 2, for which he was awarded a Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer.
He has received two National Film Awards and eight Filmfare Awards. In 2025, he received his eighth Filmfare Award for "Sajni", equalling Kishore Kumar’s record for the most wins in the Best Male Playback Singer category. In 2025, Singh received the Padma Shri, one of India’s highest civilian honours, for his contributions to the arts. During his career, Singh has sung more than 700 songs.
